publication: The Newark Herald (National Edition, NJ's largest colored weekly)
summary: Vol. 11, No. 21, 12 pages. Front page covers Montclair Housing Authority controversy, Joe Louis idle until 1939, sports (Class B tennis titles, Newark Eagles Negro League baseball), and a Newark murder suspect caught in the South. Interior pages cover the NAACP national conference in Columbus, Ohio; a Weequahic Park July 4th festival drawing ~100,000; a Springfield Avenue library exhibit on James Weldon Johnson; society/wedding pages; an editorial section eulogizing James Weldon Johnson; national amusements (Apollo, WPA theatre); sports (Galento-Lewis training, Buck Leonard/Homestead Grays, Satchell Paige to report to Newark Eagles); and a back-page churches directory plus story on four Newark policemen suspended for beating a man to death.

incidents.what: Weequahic Park festival draws crowd of about 100,000 for Independence Day observance
John A. Robinson, 38, beaten to death by Chicago police officers at Maxwell Street station; four officers later suspended
NAACP's 29th annual conference held at Shiloh Baptist Church, Columbus, Ohio, including James Weldon Johnson memorial service
Montclair civic leaders question Housing Authority's report condemning low-cost housing plan for Negro area

connections: Newark Herald editorial staff and society columnists (Julius J. Adams, Lou Blackmon, Frank Tucker) regularly cover NJ Black civic and social life alongside national wire content
Springfield Avenue branch library, Newark, held exhibit of James Weldon Johnson's books
Newark Eagles (Negro National League) coverage recurring sports feature tied to Newark's Black community
